feedback: For a mis-sort, point back to what kind of food it is and where the Eatwell Guide places it (e.g. beans go with proteins, cheese with dairy and alternatives, potatoes with starchy foods).
For 'why can't a cat make its own food?': reinforce that animals must eat; plants make food using light, but animals cannot.
If the child accepts 'humans make food from sunlight', re-run the plant-vs-animal contrast.
activities.intendedInsight: Consolidate sorting foods into food groups, linking nutrients to their functions, and the reason animals cannot make their own food.
learnerActions: Sort a set of food cards into the Eatwell Guide's five food groups, using a 'mixed foods' pile for dishes such as pizza that combine several groups.
Match each nutrient (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, plus water) to its function, and name a food that supplies several of them (e.g. milk or an egg).
Answer 'why can't a cat make its own food?' and explain in a sentence.
Spot and reject a wrong claim such as 'humans make food from sunlight'.
activities.title: Sort-and-match consolidation
